headline: Senator Tuckerman Proposes National Envelope Standard; Beige Becomes Currency of Chaos
deck: Local businesses embrace 'beige parties' as national interest in cash envelope aesthetics spirals out of control.
article:
In a move that can only be described as a bureaucratic masterpiece, Senator Clarence B. Tuckerman introduced a bill yesterday mandating that all cash envelopes bear the national seal to prevent counterfeiting. "Our currency must represent our values, and nothing screams fiscal responsibility like a well-embossed envelope of cash," declared Tuckerman, gesturing to a stack of proposed designs that bore an uncanny resemblance to women’s pantyhose packaging.

The Department of Cash Envelopes reported a staggering 200% surge in demand for pastel colors, sending economists into a tizzy over the resulting nationwide beige envelope shortage. Local artists have begun crafting black market envelopes, leading to rampant speculation that these illicit designs might somehow confer a monetary advantage. "If I can't have my cash in a beige envelope, what's even the point?" lamented local resident Sheila Dimes, clutching a crumpled green envelope as if it were a rare artifact from a bygone era.

To combat this crisis, local businesses are now organizing 'beige parties'—social gatherings designed to promote the most popular envelope color. However, these initiatives have led to widespread confusion, with many attendees mistakenly believing they were celebrating a new beige-flavored pastry trend. "I brought cupcakes, but nobody wanted them. They just stood around admiring the envelopes," reported a bewildered party organizer.

In a twist befitting the chaos of contemporary governance, the government is now considering an aesthetic committee to oversee future envelope color trends. "It's about time we take our cash aesthetics seriously," stated Tuckerman, his solemnity matched only by the looming specter of economic absurdity.
author: Eleanor Quarters, Senior Absurdity Correspondent

oped.title: Senator Tuckerman's Beige Bubble: A Cash Catastrophe in Envelopes!
oped.author: Hugh L. Hilarity, Chief Aestheticist of the Unbeige Association
oped.body: Oh, dear readers, we’ve plunged into a cash-crammed chaos thanks to Senator Tuckerman’s absurd National Envelope Standard! Beige, the color of mediocrity, now reigns supreme, forcing our vibrant local businesses into ‘beige parties.’ What’s next? ‘White Wall Wednesdays’? As a devotee of flamboyant fuchsia, I am utterly scandalized! I propose we double down on extravagance—let’s introduce a national standard for sequined envelopes! What harm could a little shimmer do? This tragedy can only be blamed on the victims' hats, which must surely detract from the serious nature of envelope aesthetics. Of course, I must reveal my own pet peeve: that gentleman in the top hat who dared swipe my favorite envelope at Gary’s. Perhaps we should regulate hats next? Colorless chaos must be met with courageously colorful solutions, darling! Let’s glitter our way to sanity!

classifieds.text: Beige envelopes, trendy and chic! Slightly used, some with light coffee stains from the last beige party. Perfect for those seeking to embrace the chaos of currency aesthetics. $2 each or $5 for a pack of three!
Desperate for an assistant to help organize cash envelopes by color and size. Must love beige, be good at math, and not mind the occasional paper cut. Pay in cash only; no checks accepted!
Lost: A lifetime supply of cash envelopes at the Great Beige Bash last Saturday. Reward for safe return: a complimentary beige-themed dinner at Gary’s Diner (checks only). Please contact me if found!

Attention all envelope enthusiasts: Beige parties have been officially designated a public health hazard. If you’ve attended, please quarantine your cash supplies and report any bizarre color-induced behavior immediately!

stories.headline: Local Retailers Embrace Beige Party Trend; Ruins Three Weddings
stories.deck: Beige has officially dethroned white as the color of choice for nuptials.
stories.article:
Following Senator Tuckerman’s national envelope standards, local entrepreneurs have jumped on the 'beige party' bandwagon, where attendees don the most drab outfits imaginable. This new movement has sent wedding planners into a frenzy, as three couples in Lavernville had to hastily swap out their pastel themes for monochrome taupe.

Experts predict that sales of beige tulle will eclipse those of traditional white by next quarter, heralding an unprecedented rise in bland-themed marriages. One officiant proclaimed, 'In beige we trust, and in excessive tedium we unite!'

stories.headline: New Documentary Explores 'The Envelope Generation'; Claims Cash Will Make a Comeback
stories.deck: Self-proclaimed historian claims cash has 'character'; rainbows of credit cards are for the emotionally weak.
stories.article:
A new documentary titled 'Crinkle & Fold: The Envelope Generation' seeks to revive interest in cash culture, featuring interviews with enthusiasts who argue that the tactile nature of envelopes rivals fine wine. Critics contend that the film glorifies fiscal nostalgia while ignoring the convenience of plastic cards, but director Buzz Wicker insists, 'Envelopes have an emotional depth that credit cards will never grasp.'

Despite the film's reception, some are already planning underground cash gatherings, where participants exchange neatly folded bills in an act they’re dubbing 'the Return to Rustic.'
